python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import colorsys

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w, h = im.size

# Sample each column's average color
cols = []
for x in range(w):
    r = g = b = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 4):
        p = im.getpixel((x, y))
        r += p[0]; g += p[1]; b += p[2]
    n = len(range(0, h, 4))
    cols.append((r//n, g//n, b//n))

# Saturation stats
sats = []
for c in cols:
    hsv = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(c[0]/255, c[1]/255, c[2]/255)
    sats.append(hsv[1])

import statistics
print("Mean saturation:", round(statistics.mean(sats), 4))
print("Median saturation:", round(statistics.median(sats), 4))
print("Max saturation:", round(max(sats), 4))
print("Columns with sat > 0.1:", sum(1 for s in sats if s > 0.1), "/", len(sats))
print("Columns with sat > 0.2:", sum(1 for s in sats if s > 0.2))

# Brightness stats
vals = [sum(c)/3 for c in cols]
print("Mean brightness:", round(statistics.mean(vals),1))
print("Min brightness:", round(min(vals),1), "Max:", round(max(vals),1))

# Where is the saturated region?
for i, s in enumerate(sats):
    if s > 0.15:
        print(f"x={i} rgb={cols[i]} sat={s:.3f}")
EOF

"**Someone like You**" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele"). She and [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)") wrote and produced the track for her second studio album, *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")* (2011). [XL Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XL_Recordings "XL Recordings") released the song as the second single from the album on 24 January 2011 (the same day the album was released) in the United Kingdom and on 9 August 2011 in the United States. Accompanied only by a piano in the song (played by co-writer Wilson), Adele sings about the end of the relationship with her ex-partner who has moved on with someone else.

"Someone like You" received universal critical acclaim, with reviewers choosing it as a highlight of *21* and praised the lyrics, its simple sound and Adele's vocal performance. It became a global success, topping the charts in nineteen countries and reaching the top 10 in various other regions. Following a universally acclaimed performance of the song at the [31st Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Brit_Awards "31st Brit Awards"), it became Adele's first number-one single in the UK and stayed atop the chart for five weeks, and was the [best-selling single of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles_by_year_in_the_United_Kingdom "List of best-selling singles by year in the United Kingdom") in the region, as well as in Ireland and Italy. It also became Adele's second number one in the US, making her the first British female solo artist in history to have two [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number ones from the same album. In July 2011, it became the first single of the decade to be certified 6× Platinum in both the UK and US. It is also certified Diamond in Canada. As of October 2025, the song has 2\.4 billion streams on Spotify, making it her most-streamed song on the platform.

The song's [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") was directed by [Jake Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Nava "Jake Nava") and filmed in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France, showing Adele walking alone through the streets. Critics praised the video for being simple and perfect for the sound of the song. As of September 2025, the video has 2\.3 billion views on YouTube. She added "Someone Like You" to the [set list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list") of her second tour [Adele Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele_Live "Adele Live"). The song has been covered by various artists, including the cast of the series *[Glee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glee_\(TV_series\) "Glee (TV series)")*. The official music video was uploaded to [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") on 30 September 2011\.

In 2012, "Someone like You" was voted the third-favourite number-one single of the last 60 years in the UK.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) "Someone like You" appeared on many year-end lists about the best songs of 2011, and was the inaugural recipient of the [Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance"), at the [54th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "54th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2012\. The song also received a nomination for the [Brit Award for British Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single") at the [32nd ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Brit_Awards "32nd Brit Awards") and also several other nominations. As of 2015[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit), "Someone like You" is the fourth best-selling single of the 21st century and is the 36th-best-selling single in the history of the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").[\[3\]](#cite_note-top_40_2015-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) "Someone Like You" has also been crowned as the UK's most popular karaoke selection for 2011 and 2012\.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Writing and inspiration

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and inspiration")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Dan_Wilson.jpg/250px-Dan_Wilson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dan_Wilson.jpg)

[Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)") (*pictured*), an American songwriter and producer co-wrote the song with Adele.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1)

"Someone like You" is about a boyfriend who broke up with Adele. She wrote it with American songwriter and producer [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)").[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) It was one of the last songs written for *21*.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) The track, which epitomizes the lyrical content of *21*, summarizes the now defunct relationship that the record is all about.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6) Adele has openly discussed the genesis of it saying, "Well, I wrote that song because I was exhausted from being such a bitch, with '[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")' or '[Rumour Has It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumour_Has_It_\(Adele_song\) "Rumour Has It (Adele song)")' ... I was really emotionally drained from the way I was portraying him, because even though I'm very bitter and regret some parts of it, he's still the most important person that's ever been in my life, and 'Someone like You,' I had to write it to feel OK with myself and OK with the two years I spent with him. And when I did it, I felt so freed."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

Adele revealed that she was struggling emotionally when she composed it: "When I was writing it I was feeling pretty miserable and pretty lonely, which I guess kind of contradicts 'Rolling in the Deep'. Whereas that was about me saying, 'I'm going to be fine without you', this is me on my knees really."[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6) She discussed further the inspiration of the song: "I can imagine being about 40 and looking for him again, only to turn up and find that he's settled with a beautiful wife and beautiful kids and he's completely happy... and I'm still on my own. The song's about that and I'm scared at the thought of that."[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6)

Adele had said that she began writing it on her acoustic guitar in the wake of the break-up of her 18-month relationship with the 30-year-old man she thought she would marry. A few months after their split, he was engaged to someone else. "We were so intense I thought we would get married. But that was something he never wanted... So when I found out he does want that with someone else, it was just the horrible-est feeling ever. But after I wrote it, I felt more at peace. It set me free... I didn't think it would resonate... with the world! I'm never gonna write a song like that again. I think that's the song I'll be known for."[\[8\]](#cite_note-Peterson1-8) She also said that "I wrote that song on the end of my bed. I had a cold. I was waiting for my bath to run. I'd found out that he'd got engaged to someone else."[\[9\]](#cite_note-Peterson2-9)

Adele took these rudimentary lyrical and musical ideas to the recording session with Wilson, where the two sat around the piano to try out various melodies and lyrics.[\[10\]](#cite_note-KMTT-10) They decided to keep the musical production sparse: "We just wrote it on the piano and then we recorded it when it was written. It wasn't sort of like recording it and listening to it thinking 'where can we go next?' It was really old school."[\[10\]](#cite_note-KMTT-10) During an interview with *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*, Wilson stated that while writing the song, they wanted to make it as personal as possible.[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11) He added "We didn't try to make it open-ended so it could apply to 'anybody.' We tried to make it as personal as possible. She may not have had a melodic hook or a specific lyrical idea, but she always knew what she wanted to say. She definitely had a master plan."[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11) The song was recorded at Harmony Studios in West [Hollywood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_California "Hollywood, California") with Wilson playing piano and Philip Allen as engineer.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) The [mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") was done by [Tom Elmhirst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Elmhirst "Tom Elmhirst") and [Dan Parry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Parry "Dan Parry") while the [mastering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mastering "Audio mastering") was finished by Tom Coyne.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1)

> "\[...\] 'Someone like You,' the stirring, somber closer in which Adele goes to visit a former love (with high hopes of a reconciliation), only to discover he has not only moved on with his life, but is in a much better place. And though she's heartbroken, she puts on a brave face, stubbornly proclaiming she'll find someone just like him, even if she knows that she never will. And that conclusion makes you ache not only because it's so daunting, but because it's so real. We've all felt that way, tried to trick ourselves into thinking that any other outcome was possible. In Adele's music, much like life, there are no happy endings."

— James Montgomery of MTV News talking about "Someone like You".[\[12\]](#cite_note-mtvpain-12)

According to sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by [Sony Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Publishing "Sony Music Publishing"), "Someone like You" is a slow tempo of 67\.5 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute").[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) Written in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time"), the song is in the key of [A major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_major "A major").[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) The song follows three chord progressions. Adele's vocal range spans from [F♯3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)") to [E5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_\(musical_note\) "E (musical note)") during the song.[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) A slow, plaintive ballad pairing Adele's voice with a looping piano line, "Someone like You" is the lyrical opposite of "[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")"[\[14\]](#cite_note-Adkins2011locSomeoneLikeYou-14) on which the singer narrates coming to terms with the end of the relationship:[\[14\]](#cite_note-Adkins2011locSomeoneLikeYou-14) "Nevermind, I'll find someone like you/I wish nothing but the best for you, too/Don't forget me, I beg/I'll remember you said/Sometimes it lasts in love, but sometimes it hurts instead." According to Sean Fennessey of *[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Village_Voice "The Village Voice")*, the singer's "nuanced"[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) voice goes up a full [octave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octave "Octave") and "into a near-shrieked whisper" as she sings parts of the chorus.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) However, she "rebounds and gathers herself", and her voice descends into its fuller and more melancholy state.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) Critics praised its introspective lyrics and maturity.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-17) "Someone like You" has been compared to the song "[Hometown Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hometown_Glory "Hometown Glory")" (2008) from the album *[19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/19_\(Adele_album\) "19 (Adele album)")*.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16) John Murphy of *[MusicOMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicOMH "MusicOMH")* said that the song "casts Adele as the spurned lover, turning up outside her ex's house, now moved on and settled down, begging for a second chance."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) According to Aamir Yaqub of Soul Culture, "Talking of a lost love, this an extremely touching track with a vocal performance that makes the narrative almost tangible ... It really captures the experience of the story and puts it across in both a credible and incredible fashion."[\[19\]](#cite_note-soulculture1-19) Cameron Adams of *[Herald Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herald_Sun "Herald Sun")* called the song a "spine-tingling sparse piano ballad."[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

Lyrically, the song talks about the end of Adele's first "real relationship", which was with her long-time friend and lover, and it shows her confronting his marriage.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-rollshow-22) At the beginning of the song, she sings the lines "I heard that you're settled down/That you found a girl and you're married now. I heard that your dreams came true/Guess she gave you things I couldn't give to you" with a soft voice and accompanied just by a simple piano melody.[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11)[\[23\]](#cite_note-herald-23) The lyrics of "Someone like You" are talking about what once was and what could have been as stated by a writer of *[Daily Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Herald_\(Arlington_Heights\) "Daily Herald (Arlington Heights)")*.[\[23\]](#cite_note-herald-23) Finding the strength to bounce back from hardship and heartache, Adele sings the lines, "Never mind, I'll find someone like you. I wish nothing but the best for you, too/Don't forget me, I beg, I remember you said/Sometimes it lasts in love but sometimes it hurts instead."[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) Talking about the meaning and the composition of the song, Jer Fairall of [PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters") said: "The song's subject—Adele mentally addressing an old lover who has since found happiness elsewhere—is familiar, but the detail she colors it with are vibrantly tactile and resonant, from the sense-memory setting of 'we were born and raised in a summer haze' to her recollection of his cruel kiss-off line 'I remember you said, 'sometimes it lasts in love and sometimes it hurts instead' and how she comes to take solace in the statement as an empowering mantra."[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25) During her concert tour in August 2024, Adele revealed that this song had changed her life.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Upon release, the song received widespread acclaim from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_critics "Music critics"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) with many citing it as the highlight of *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")*. In a track-by-track review for *21*, Joanne Dorken of MTV UK noted the track's placement at the end of the album saying, "It maybe a cliché, but Adele has saved the best until last with this heartfelt and enchanting piano ballad. ... It's sad but beautiful and displays Adele at her best – marking the perfect end to what has been in our eyes, a faultless album."[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16) Will Dean of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* claimed the song was the album's "highlight", characterizing it as "gorgeous".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) That was echoed by [*Slant* Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slant_Magazine "Slant Magazine")'s Matthew Cole who also called the song "gorgeous".[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")*'s Chris Parkin also marked the song as a highlight, describing it as "surprisingly weighty" and comparing it favorably to the work of American [Country blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_blues "Country blues") singer [Karen Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Dalton "Karen Dalton").[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

Tom Breihan of [Pitchfork Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_Media "Pitchfork Media") selected "Someone like You" as a song of the day, claiming it served as a reaffirmation of popular music: "Sometimes, pop music can still break your heart."[\[17\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-17) Writing for [BBC Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Online "BBC Online"), Ian Wade noted that the "final track Someone Like You, just voice and piano, is an actual thing of beauty, placing the listener in one of those moments where you feel you're in the presence of a future standard."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Bill Lamb of [About.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About.com "About.com") wrote that "the piano melody is gorgeous and combined with Adele's heartfelt reading of her words, the effect is highly emotional. You can imagine it being both honked through by talent show contestants and transcended by veterans alike."[\[32\]](#cite_note-about-32) Lamb went to write that the song is one of the "top songs of 2011" and that "romantic pain has rarely been so utterly beautiful."[\[32\]](#cite_note-about-32) Jer Fairall of PopMatters called the song "absolute magic" and praised Adele's performance by saying, "Though it is unquestionably her finest vocal showcase to date, it is less remarkable for its more powerful moments than for the small ones where her voice dips, with rueful melancholy on the line 'I heard that your dreams came true' or cracks on the 'I beg' in the chorus, like she's startled at the revelation of her own vulnerability."[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25) He further called her vocal performance of the song "stunning" and "finally worthy of her talents".[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25)

Writing for the website No Ripcord, Gary McGinley said that the song "has an aching beauty and the hallmarks of a modern standard."[\[33\]](#cite_note-ripcord-33) He further added that it "sounds poised to soundtrack atmospheric TV trailers over the coming months."[\[33\]](#cite_note-ripcord-33) A writer of [*URB* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/URB_\(magazine\) "URB (magazine)") called "Someone like You" "a heart-wrencher made all the more real by reeling phrasing and bare-voiced pleading, 'I wish nothing but the best for you, too.'"[\[34\]](#cite_note-urb-34) John Murphy of *MusicOMH* categorized "Someone like You" and "[Turning Tables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turning_Tables "Turning Tables")" as "the two best songs on the album."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) He concluded that the song was "desperately sad and utterly, utterly gorgeous."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) Bary Walters of *[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")* wrote that on "the piano-led finale, she vows, 'I'll find someone like you,' as if that's progress. It's a statement that's utterly WTF and yet true to the cyclical nature of psychological damage."[\[35\]](#cite_note-Spin-35) Sputnikmusic's Joseph Viney called the song "an ode to stalking with a perverse attitude that lies underneath the fragile composition, looks set to become the soundtrack to a million messy break-ups."[\[36\]](#cite_note-Sputnik-36) Allison Stewart of *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* put the song on her list "Recommended tracks".[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

*[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Village_Voice "The Village Voice")*'s [Pazz & Jop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazz_&_Jop "Pazz & Jop") annual critics' poll of the best songs of 2011 ranked "Someone like You" at number nine; Adele's previous single "Rolling in the Deep" topped the same critics' poll. In 2019, *[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")*,[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*,[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) and *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")*[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) ranked the song as the 39th, 64th, and 71st best song of the 2010s, respectively. *[Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parade_\(magazine\) "Parade (magazine)")* and *[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")* both ranked the song number six on their lists of Adele's greatest songs.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)[\[42\]](#cite_note-42)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Someone like You" achieved international commercial success, topping the [record charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart") in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States, as well as reaching the top ten in many other countries. The song debuted at number 36 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") in late-January 2011 due to strong digital downloads from *21*. Following a live performance of the song at the 2011 BRIT Awards, it climbed 46 places from the previous week to number one, beating [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s single "[Born This Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_This_Way_\(song\) "Born This Way (song)")" (2011), although it was at number 18 on the mid-week chart update.[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43) While "Someone like You" was at number one on the chart, Adele's previous single, "Rolling in the Deep" was placed at number four.[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43) With that achievement, Adele has become the first living artist since [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") in 1964 who simultaneously had two top five hits in both the charts (*21* and *19* were also in the top five on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart")).[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43)[\[44\]](#cite_note-44)[\[45\]](#cite_note-hot100peak2-45) It stayed atop the chart for four consecutive weeks before slipping to number two on 26 March.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) Following a performance on [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief "Comic Relief"), the song returned to number one for a fifth week.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) It has been certified 6× Platinum by the [BPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry"), denoting sales and streams of 3,600,000 units.[\[48\]](#cite_note-bpi-48) On 5 July 2011, it was announced that the song had sold 1 million copies in the UK, becoming the first single of the decade to reach the threshold and the sixteenth song released in the 21st century to do so.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49)[\[50\]](#cite_note-50) It became the biggest selling single of 2011 in the United Kingdom, selling over 1,240,000 copies. By June 2015, UK sales stood at 1,570,000 copies, making "Someone like You" the second best-selling single of the 2010s and the third-best-seller of the 21st century.[\[3\]](#cite_note-top_40_2015-3) As of November 2015, the song has sold 1,584,000 copies in the UK.[\[51\]](#cite_note-Nov_2015_UK-51)

In [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Official_Finnish_Charts "The Official Finnish Charts"), "Someone like You" debuted at number 14 in October 2011 and rose to number one in its 12th week in early 2012—the week when Adele had three simultaneous top-ten songs ("[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")" at number two and "[Set Fire to the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_Fire_to_the_Rain "Set Fire to the Rain")" at number seven).[\[52\]](#cite_note-finnish-chart-procession-52)[\[53\]](#cite_note-finnish-chart-2/2012-53) In France, despite not having been certified, "Someone like You" has sold 350,800 copies and became one of the best-selling singles in the country.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) The song debuted at number 47 on the [Australian Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts").[\[55\]](#cite_note-aus-55) "Someone like You" remained at the top position of the chart for seven consecutive weeks[\[55\]](#cite_note-aus-55) and it was certified 4× Platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") (ARIA).[\[56\]](#cite_note-auscert-56) It has also peaked at number one in New Zealand for five weeks, ending an 11-week run at number one for "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")".[\[57\]](#cite_note-nz-57)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/18/Someone_like_you_music_video_screenshot.jpg/250px-Someone_like_you_music_video_screenshot.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Someone_like_you_music_video_screenshot.jpg)

Adele walking alone in Paris in the black-and-white music video for "Someone like You"

The [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for the song was filmed in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") by English director [Jake Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Nava "Jake Nava")[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68) who said:[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68)[\[69\]](#cite_note-69)

> The location evokes style and romance. And shooting early in the morning allows you to focus on Adele in this lonely and emotional space.

The video begins with a shot of a road in Paris and Adele is seen walking on it alone. She continues to walk and starts singing the song with a sad look as the camera makes circles and shots more locations in Paris including the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower"). During the second chorus, Adele stops singing and pauses on the [Pont Alexandre III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pont_Alexandre_III "Pont Alexandre III") to look over the [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine "Seine"). She continues walking through the deserted streets during the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge (music)") before finally entering a building in which she sees her ex-lover.[\[70\]](#cite_note-ewvideo-70) After seeing her, he starts to walk away and several shots of Adele looking at him follow.

The video premiered on [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") and [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") on 29 September 2011,[\[12\]](#cite_note-mtvpain-12)[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71) It received glowing reviews from music critics; James Montgomery of MTV News called the video "a somber, black-and-white affair, featuring Adele wandering the early morning streets and pining for her long-lost love. It's a perfect match for the song's jaw-dropping emotional range—raw and unfiltered and incredibly sad but also, in a lot of ways, beautiful and resolute."[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68) In another review of the video he praised its black-and-white shots saying that "director Jake Nava made the smart decision to shoot it in arty, smudgy black-and-white, which only adds to the clip's desolate, haunted feel."[\[12\]](#cite_note-mtvpain-12) He added that "there are no special effects, no camera tricks or elaborate choreography, because those are quick fixes" and called Adele the "Queen of Pain."[\[12\]](#cite_note-mtvpain-12) A writer of the website [HitFix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HitFix "HitFix") concluded that the video is "in keeping with the singer's subdued style" and added that its vibe fits with the "melancholy tune."[\[72\]](#cite_note-hitfix-72) *[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")*'s Tanner Stransky called the video "quiet" and said that "it's just what you'd want to see for this break-up heart-wrencher."[\[70\]](#cite_note-ewvideo-70) Krista Wick of *[Entertainment Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Tonight "Entertainment Tonight")* praised the video for being "more than enough to accompany Adele's soulful vocals."[\[73\]](#cite_note-73)

Amanda Dobbins of [*New York* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_\(magazine\) "New York (magazine)") concluded that "the secretly devastating video" for "Someone like You" will remind Adele's ex-lover what he has done by leaving her.[\[74\]](#cite_note-74) A writer of *[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Huffington_Post "The Huffington Post")* praised the simplicity and the sadness in the video.[\[75\]](#cite_note-75) Sarah Dean of the same publication called it an "uncomplicated, moving film" and wrote, "the video is nothing more than Adele wandering around the deserted city of love alone, under its grey skies, singing her sorrowful notes, but because it's her, we don't need any more."[\[76\]](#cite_note-76) That was echoed by Jason Lipshutz of [*Billboard* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)") who said that the video was "as simply constructed as the song's vocal-and-piano arrangement."[\[77\]](#cite_note-77) Marc Hogan of *Spin* said that the scene in which Adele looks in the camera, "speak\[s\] for itself" about the sadness in the video.[\[78\]](#cite_note-78) Andrew Matson of *[The Seattle Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Seattle_Times "The Seattle Times")* said, "the song of the year now has a simple, perfect video: Adele in Paris, singing and strolling, apparently processing the breakup detailed in the song's lyrics. The look on her face during the 'I wish nothing but the best for you' line is the best, just gutting, a real achievement how she plays it cold but not sarcastic. I think in times of emotional devastation, everyone wants stand on a bridge over the Seine on a cold day, squinting into the wind, sorting it out."[\[79\]](#cite_note-79)

A writer of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* wrote: "this clip for the ballad 'Someone Like You' sticks to the singer's simple but emotionally direct approach with black-and-white footage that lingers on her subtly expressive face as she lip-synchs to the tune while walking along sad, grey city streets."[\[80\]](#cite_note-80) Andrea Devaro of *[Long Island Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island_Press "Long Island Press")* concluded, "its simplicity beautifully portrays the complexity of emotions invoked in the song."[\[81\]](#cite_note-81) Leah Collins of *[Dose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dose_\(magazine\) "Dose (magazine)")* called Adele "'60s bombshell glam" and said that the video's "simplicity is its strength."[\[82\]](#cite_note-collinsdose-82) She added: "There's something about streetlamps, cafes and the River Seine that lend an air of melancholic elegance to what would otherwise be just another walk of shame by a girl with two-day-old hair. Not everyone gets to indulge in moments as tragic but beautiful as a weepy solitary walk through Paris landmarks. But then, we don't all have voices as tragic and beautiful as Adele's either."[\[82\]](#cite_note-collinsdose-82) A more mixed review was given by [AOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL "AOL")'s Ashley Percival who called the video predictable and added "It's all very pleasant, but after all this time, what's the point?".[\[83\]](#cite_note-83) Nicole Eggenberger of *[OK!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK! "OK!")* wrote that Adele "created the perfect music video to go along with her hauntingly beautiful ballad" and further described it as "simple yet stunning."[\[84\]](#cite_note-84)

At the 2011 [Q Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q_Awards "Q Awards"), "Someone like You" was nominated in the category for Best Track.[\[85\]](#cite_note-85) The song was also nominated in the category for Best Song at the 2011 [Music of Black Origin Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Black_Origin_Awards "Music of Black Origin Awards").[\[86\]](#cite_note-86) "Someone like You" won the first [Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance"), at the [54th Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Grammy_Awards "2012 Grammy Awards"), which were held on 12 February 2012\.[\[87\]](#cite_note-87)[\[88\]](#cite_note-88) Song also nominated for [Brit Award for British Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single") at the [32nd Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Brit_Awards "32nd Brit Awards"), but lost to "[What Makes You Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Makes_You_Beautiful "What Makes You Beautiful")" by [One Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Direction "One Direction").[\[89\]](#cite_note-89)

"**Someone like You**" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele"). She and [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)") wrote and produced the track for her second studio album, *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")* (2011). [XL Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XL_Recordings "XL Recordings") released the song as the second single from the album on 24 January 2011 (the same day the album was released) in the United Kingdom and on 9 August 2011 in the United States. Accompanied only by a piano in the song (played by co-writer Wilson), Adele sings about the end of the relationship with her ex-partner who has moved on with someone else.

"Someone like You" received universal critical acclaim, with reviewers choosing it as a highlight of *21* and praised the lyrics, its simple sound and Adele's vocal performance. It became a global success, topping the charts in nineteen countries and reaching the top 10 in various other regions. Following a universally acclaimed performance of the song at the [31st Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Brit_Awards "31st Brit Awards"), it became Adele's first number-one single in the UK and stayed atop the chart for five weeks, and was the [best-selling single of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles_by_year_in_the_United_Kingdom "List of best-selling singles by year in the United Kingdom") in the region, as well as in Ireland and Italy. It also became Adele's second number one in the US, making her the first British female solo artist in history to have two [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number ones from the same album. In July 2011, it became the first single of the decade to be certified 6× Platinum in both the UK and US. It is also certified Diamond in Canada. As of October 2025, the song has 2\.4 billion streams on Spotify, making it her most-streamed song on the platform.

The song's [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") was directed by [Jake Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Nava "Jake Nava") and filmed in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France, showing Adele walking alone through the streets. Critics praised the video for being simple and perfect for the sound of the song. As of September 2025, the video has 2\.3 billion views on YouTube. She added "Someone Like You" to the [set list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list") of her second tour [Adele Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele_Live "Adele Live"). The song has been covered by various artists, including the cast of the series *[Glee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glee_\(TV_series\) "Glee (TV series)")*. The official music video was uploaded to [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") on 30 September 2011\.

In 2012, "Someone like You" was voted the third-favourite number-one single of the last 60 years in the UK.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) "Someone like You" appeared on many year-end lists about the best songs of 2011, and was the inaugural recipient of the [Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance"), at the [54th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "54th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2012\. The song also received a nomination for the [Brit Award for British Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single") at the [32nd ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Brit_Awards "32nd Brit Awards") and also several other nominations. As of 2015[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit), "Someone like You" is the fourth best-selling single of the 21st century and is the 36th-best-selling single in the history of the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").[\[3\]](#cite_note-top_40_2015-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) "Someone Like You" has also been crowned as the UK's most popular karaoke selection for 2011 and 2012\.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Writing and inspiration

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and inspiration")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Dan_Wilson.jpg/250px-Dan_Wilson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dan_Wilson.jpg)

[Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)") (*pictured*), an American songwriter and producer co-wrote the song with Adele.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1)

"Someone like You" is about a boyfriend who broke up with Adele. She wrote it with American songwriter and producer [Dan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Wilson_\(musician\) "Dan Wilson (musician)").[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) It was one of the last songs written for *21*.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) The track, which epitomizes the lyrical content of *21*, summarizes the now defunct relationship that the record is all about.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6) Adele has openly discussed the genesis of it saying, "Well, I wrote that song because I was exhausted from being such a bitch, with '[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")' or '[Rumour Has It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumour_Has_It_\(Adele_song\) "Rumour Has It (Adele song)")' ... I was really emotionally drained from the way I was portraying him, because even though I'm very bitter and regret some parts of it, he's still the most important person that's ever been in my life, and 'Someone like You,' I had to write it to feel OK with myself and OK with the two years I spent with him. And when I did it, I felt so freed."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

Adele revealed that she was struggling emotionally when she composed it: "When I was writing it I was feeling pretty miserable and pretty lonely, which I guess kind of contradicts 'Rolling in the Deep'. Whereas that was about me saying, 'I'm going to be fine without you', this is me on my knees really."[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6) She discussed further the inspiration of the song: "I can imagine being about 40 and looking for him again, only to turn up and find that he's settled with a beautiful wife and beautiful kids and he's completely happy... and I'm still on my own. The song's about that and I'm scared at the thought of that."[\[6\]](#cite_note-Levine-6)

Adele had said that she began writing it on her acoustic guitar in the wake of the break-up of her 18-month relationship with the 30-year-old man she thought she would marry. A few months after their split, he was engaged to someone else. "We were so intense I thought we would get married. But that was something he never wanted... So when I found out he does want that with someone else, it was just the horrible-est feeling ever. But after I wrote it, I felt more at peace. It set me free... I didn't think it would resonate... with the world! I'm never gonna write a song like that again. I think that's the song I'll be known for."[\[8\]](#cite_note-Peterson1-8) She also said that "I wrote that song on the end of my bed. I had a cold. I was waiting for my bath to run. I'd found out that he'd got engaged to someone else."[\[9\]](#cite_note-Peterson2-9)

Adele took these rudimentary lyrical and musical ideas to the recording session with Wilson, where the two sat around the piano to try out various melodies and lyrics.[\[10\]](#cite_note-KMTT-10) They decided to keep the musical production sparse: "We just wrote it on the piano and then we recorded it when it was written. It wasn't sort of like recording it and listening to it thinking 'where can we go next?' It was really old school."[\[10\]](#cite_note-KMTT-10) During an interview with *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*, Wilson stated that while writing the song, they wanted to make it as personal as possible.[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11) He added "We didn't try to make it open-ended so it could apply to 'anybody.' We tried to make it as personal as possible. She may not have had a melodic hook or a specific lyrical idea, but she always knew what she wanted to say. She definitely had a master plan."[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11) The song was recorded at Harmony Studios in West [Hollywood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_California "Hollywood, California") with Wilson playing piano and Philip Allen as engineer.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1) The [mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") was done by [Tom Elmhirst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Elmhirst "Tom Elmhirst") and [Dan Parry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Parry "Dan Parry") while the [mastering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mastering "Audio mastering") was finished by Tom Coyne.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Booklet-1)

> "\[...\] 'Someone like You,' the stirring, somber closer in which Adele goes to visit a former love (with high hopes of a reconciliation), only to discover he has not only moved on with his life, but is in a much better place. And though she's heartbroken, she puts on a brave face, stubbornly proclaiming she'll find someone just like him, even if she knows that she never will. And that conclusion makes you ache not only because it's so daunting, but because it's so real. We've all felt that way, tried to trick ourselves into thinking that any other outcome was possible. In Adele's music, much like life, there are no happy endings."

— James Montgomery of MTV News talking about "Someone like You".[\[12\]](#cite_note-mtvpain-12)

According to sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by [Sony Music Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Publishing "Sony Music Publishing"), "Someone like You" is a slow tempo of 67\.5 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute").[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) Written in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time"), the song is in the key of [A major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_major "A major").[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) The song follows three chord progressions. Adele's vocal range spans from [F♯3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F♯_\(musical_note\) "F♯ (musical note)") to [E5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_\(musical_note\) "E (musical note)") during the song.[\[13\]](#cite_note-musicnotes-13) A slow, plaintive ballad pairing Adele's voice with a looping piano line, "Someone like You" is the lyrical opposite of "[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")"[\[14\]](#cite_note-Adkins2011locSomeoneLikeYou-14) on which the singer narrates coming to terms with the end of the relationship:[\[14\]](#cite_note-Adkins2011locSomeoneLikeYou-14) "Nevermind, I'll find someone like you/I wish nothing but the best for you, too/Don't forget me, I beg/I'll remember you said/Sometimes it lasts in love, but sometimes it hurts instead." According to Sean Fennessey of *[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Village_Voice "The Village Voice")*, the singer's "nuanced"[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) voice goes up a full [octave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octave "Octave") and "into a near-shrieked whisper" as she sings parts of the chorus.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) However, she "rebounds and gathers herself", and her voice descends into its fuller and more melancholy state.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Village-15) Critics praised its introspective lyrics and maturity.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-17) "Someone like You" has been compared to the song "[Hometown Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hometown_Glory "Hometown Glory")" (2008) from the album *[19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/19_\(Adele_album\) "19 (Adele album)")*.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16) John Murphy of *[MusicOMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicOMH "MusicOMH")* said that the song "casts Adele as the spurned lover, turning up outside her ex's house, now moved on and settled down, begging for a second chance."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) According to Aamir Yaqub of Soul Culture, "Talking of a lost love, this an extremely touching track with a vocal performance that makes the narrative almost tangible ... It really captures the experience of the story and puts it across in both a credible and incredible fashion."[\[19\]](#cite_note-soulculture1-19) Cameron Adams of *[Herald Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herald_Sun "Herald Sun")* called the song a "spine-tingling sparse piano ballad."[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

Lyrically, the song talks about the end of Adele's first "real relationship", which was with her long-time friend and lover, and it shows her confronting his marriage.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-rollshow-22) At the beginning of the song, she sings the lines "I heard that you're settled down/That you found a girl and you're married now. I heard that your dreams came true/Guess she gave you things I couldn't give to you" with a soft voice and accompanied just by a simple piano melody.[\[11\]](#cite_note-bil1005-11)[\[23\]](#cite_note-herald-23) The lyrics of "Someone like You" are talking about what once was and what could have been as stated by a writer of *[Daily Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Herald_\(Arlington_Heights\) "Daily Herald (Arlington Heights)")*.[\[23\]](#cite_note-herald-23) Finding the strength to bounce back from hardship and heartache, Adele sings the lines, "Never mind, I'll find someone like you. I wish nothing but the best for you, too/Don't forget me, I beg, I remember you said/Sometimes it lasts in love but sometimes it hurts instead."[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) Talking about the meaning and the composition of the song, Jer Fairall of [PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters") said: "The song's subject—Adele mentally addressing an old lover who has since found happiness elsewhere—is familiar, but the detail she colors it with are vibrantly tactile and resonant, from the sense-memory setting of 'we were born and raised in a summer haze' to her recollection of his cruel kiss-off line 'I remember you said, 'sometimes it lasts in love and sometimes it hurts instead' and how she comes to take solace in the statement as an empowering mantra."[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25) During her concert tour in August 2024, Adele revealed that this song had changed her life.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Upon release, the song received widespread acclaim from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_critics "Music critics"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) with many citing it as the highlight of *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")*. In a track-by-track review for *21*, Joanne Dorken of MTV UK noted the track's placement at the end of the album saying, "It maybe a cliché, but Adele has saved the best until last with this heartfelt and enchanting piano ballad. ... It's sad but beautiful and displays Adele at her best – marking the perfect end to what has been in our eyes, a faultless album."[\[16\]](#cite_note-Dorken-16) Will Dean of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* claimed the song was the album's "highlight", characterizing it as "gorgeous".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) That was echoed by [*Slant* Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slant_Magazine "Slant Magazine")'s Matthew Cole who also called the song "gorgeous".[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")*'s Chris Parkin also marked the song as a highlight, describing it as "surprisingly weighty" and comparing it favorably to the work of American [Country blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_blues "Country blues") singer [Karen Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Dalton "Karen Dalton").[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

Tom Breihan of [Pitchfork Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_Media "Pitchfork Media") selected "Someone like You" as a song of the day, claiming it served as a reaffirmation of popular music: "Sometimes, pop music can still break your heart."[\[17\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-17) Writing for [BBC Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Online "BBC Online"), Ian Wade noted that the "final track Someone Like You, just voice and piano, is an actual thing of beauty, placing the listener in one of those moments where you feel you're in the presence of a future standard."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Bill Lamb of [About.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About.com "About.com") wrote that "the piano melody is gorgeous and combined with Adele's heartfelt reading of her words, the effect is highly emotional. You can imagine it being both honked through by talent show contestants and transcended by veterans alike."[\[32\]](#cite_note-about-32) Lamb went to write that the song is one of the "top songs of 2011" and that "romantic pain has rarely been so utterly beautiful."[\[32\]](#cite_note-about-32) Jer Fairall of PopMatters called the song "absolute magic" and praised Adele's performance by saying, "Though it is unquestionably her finest vocal showcase to date, it is less remarkable for its more powerful moments than for the small ones where her voice dips, with rueful melancholy on the line 'I heard that your dreams came true' or cracks on the 'I beg' in the chorus, like she's startled at the revelation of her own vulnerability."[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25) He further called her vocal performance of the song "stunning" and "finally worthy of her talents".[\[25\]](#cite_note-popmatters-25)

Writing for the website No Ripcord, Gary McGinley said that the song "has an aching beauty and the hallmarks of a modern standard."[\[33\]](#cite_note-ripcord-33) He further added that it "sounds poised to soundtrack atmospheric TV trailers over the coming months."[\[33\]](#cite_note-ripcord-33) A writer of [*URB* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/URB_\(magazine\) "URB (magazine)") called "Someone like You" "a heart-wrencher made all the more real by reeling phrasing and bare-voiced pleading, 'I wish nothing but the best for you, too.'"[\[34\]](#cite_note-urb-34) John Murphy of *MusicOMH* categorized "Someone like You" and "[Turning Tables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turning_Tables "Turning Tables")" as "the two best songs on the album."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) He concluded that the song was "desperately sad and utterly, utterly gorgeous."[\[18\]](#cite_note-OMH-18) Bary Walters of *[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")* wrote that on "the piano-led finale, she vows, 'I'll find someone like you,' as if that's progress. It's a statement that's utterly WTF and yet true to the cyclical nature of psychological damage."[\[35\]](#cite_note-Spin-35) Sputnikmusic's Joseph Viney called the song "an ode to stalking with a perverse attitude that lies underneath the fragile composition, looks set to become the soundtrack to a million messy break-ups."[\[36\]](#cite_note-Sputnik-36) Allison Stewart of *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* put the song on her list "Recommended tracks".[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

*[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Village_Voice "The Village Voice")*'s [Pazz & Jop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazz_&_Jop "Pazz & Jop") annual critics' poll of the best songs of 2011 ranked "Someone like You" at number nine; Adele's previous single "Rolling in the Deep" topped the same critics' poll. In 2019, *[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")*,[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*,[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) and *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")*[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) ranked the song as the 39th, 64th, and 71st best song of the 2010s, respectively. *[Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parade_\(magazine\) "Parade (magazine)")* and *[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")* both ranked the song number six on their lists of Adele's greatest songs.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)[\[42\]](#cite_note-42)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Someone like You" achieved international commercial success, topping the [record charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart") in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States, as well as reaching the top ten in many other countries. The song debuted at number 36 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") in late-January 2011 due to strong digital downloads from *21*. Following a live performance of the song at the 2011 BRIT Awards, it climbed 46 places from the previous week to number one, beating [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s single "[Born This Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_This_Way_\(song\) "Born This Way (song)")" (2011), although it was at number 18 on the mid-week chart update.[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43) While "Someone like You" was at number one on the chart, Adele's previous single, "Rolling in the Deep" was placed at number four.[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43) With that achievement, Adele has become the first living artist since [The Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") in 1964 who simultaneously had two top five hits in both the charts (*21* and *19* were also in the top five on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart")).[\[43\]](#cite_note-achievement-43)[\[44\]](#cite_note-44)[\[45\]](#cite_note-hot100peak2-45) It stayed atop the chart for four consecutive weeks before slipping to number two on 26 March.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) Following a performance on [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief "Comic Relief"), the song returned to number one for a fifth week.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) It has been certified 6× Platinum by the [BPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry"), denoting sales and streams of 3,600,000 units.[\[48\]](#cite_note-bpi-48) On 5 July 2011, it was announced that the song had sold 1 million copies in the UK, becoming the first single of the decade to reach the threshold and the sixteenth song released in the 21st century to do so.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49)[\[50\]](#cite_note-50) It became the biggest selling single of 2011 in the United Kingdom, selling over 1,240,000 copies. By June 2015, UK sales stood at 1,570,000 copies, making "Someone like You" the second best-selling single of the 2010s and the third-best-seller of the 21st century.[\[3\]](#cite_note-top_40_2015-3) As of November 2015, the song has sold 1,584,000 copies in the UK.[\[51\]](#cite_note-Nov_2015_UK-51)

In [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Official_Finnish_Charts "The Official Finnish Charts"), "Someone like You" debuted at number 14 in October 2011 and rose to number one in its 12th week in early 2012—the week when Adele had three simultaneous top-ten songs ("[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")" at number two and "[Set Fire to the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_Fire_to_the_Rain "Set Fire to the Rain")" at number seven).[\[52\]](#cite_note-finnish-chart-procession-52)[\[53\]](#cite_note-finnish-chart-2/2012-53) In France, despite not having been certified, "Someone like You" has sold 350,800 copies and became one of the best-selling singles in the country.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) The song debuted at number 47 on the [Australian Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts").[\[55\]](#cite_note-aus-55) "Someone like You" remained at the top position of the chart for seven consecutive weeks[\[55\]](#cite_note-aus-55) and it was certified 4× Platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") (ARIA).[\[56\]](#cite_note-auscert-56) It has also peaked at number one in New Zealand for five weeks, ending an 11-week run at number one for "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")".[\[57\]](#cite_note-nz-57)

The [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for the song was filmed in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") by English director [Jake Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Nava "Jake Nava")[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68) who said:[\[68\]](#cite_note-videopremiere-68)[\[69\]](#cite_note-69)

"All of Me" is a song by American singer John Legend from his fourth studio album Love in the Future (2013). It is dedicated to Legend's wife Chrissy Teigen.     "All of Me" first aired on American mainstream urban radio as the album's third single on August 12, 2013.

On the week ending May 17, 2014, it peaked at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming his first number-one single in the United States. It knocked off "Happy" by Pharrell Williams, which had spent 10 weeks at number one. The song peaked at number two in the United Kingdom, South Africa and New Zealand and topped the charts in Australia, Canada, Ireland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands. It became the second best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 4.67 million copies sold for the year,[1] as well as the third best-selling song in the United Kingdom.[2] "All of Me" was the third best-selling song of 2014 with 12.3 million equivalent-units worldwide (sales plus streaming), according to the IFPI.[3]

A remix of the song (Tiësto's Birthday Treatment remix), featuring EDM artist Tiësto, was released in January 2014 and won the 2015 Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical, while another remix was done in March of that year by trance artist Dash Berlin. A live version of the song was nominated for Best Pop Solo Performance, losing to Williams' "Happy".[4]

Background and composition[edit]
"All of Me" is a piano ballad, which was inspired by his then-fiancée, now wife, model Chrissy Teigen.[5] The couple met in 2007 on the set of his video for "Stereo". They were then married on September 14, 2013.[6] The song was produced by Dave Tozer and Legend himself.[7] It is a simple, modest proposal set against delicate keys.[8]

Sheet music for "All of Me" shows the key of A♭ major with a slow tempo of 63 beats per minute. Vocals span from C3 to B♭4.[9]

Release and promotion[edit]
In June 2013, Legend premiered "All of Me" during a performance on Oprah Winfrey's Oprah's Next Chapter.[10] On August 6, 2013, the full song was released to iTunes along with the pre-order for Love in the Future.[5][11] "All of Me" impacted American mainstream urban radio as the third single from Love in the Future on August 12, 2013.[12]

Dutch electronic producer Tiësto released a remix of the song in January 2014.[4] A country-influenced duet version of "All of Me" with Jennifer Nettles, featuring Hunter Hayes on guitar, was released in June 2014.[13]

Commercial performance[edit]
After being stationary at number two for six weeks, "All of Me" finally reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated May 17, 2014. This was Legend's first Hot 100 number one single, almost 10 years since his first appearance on the chart. That was the longest wait for an artist's first number-one song from their first chart appearance since Snoop Dogg waited 10 years and 10 months for his.[14][15] "All of Me" became the second best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 4.67 million copies sold for the year. The song spent three weeks at number one before being dethroned by Iggy Azalea's "Fancy" featuring Charli XCX.[1] Additionally, "All of Me" spent 23 consecutive weeks in the Billboard Hot 100's top 10 and spent an overall 59 non-consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.[16] As of April 2016, "All of Me" has sold 5,878,000 copies cumulatively in the United States.[17]

In the United Kingdom, "All of Me" peaked at number two on the UK Singles Chart,[18] and it became the third best-selling song of 2014 in the UK.[2] As of February 2016, the song has sold 1.18 million copies in the UK.[19]

Critical reception[edit]
"All of Me" was met with generally positive reviews from music critics. Ken Capobianco of The Boston Globe named the song the album's "essential track".[20] Ryan Patrick of Exclaim! said the song, shows "Legend's current commercially friendly, sentimental sound."[21] Jon Dolan of Rolling Stone called the song a "mountainous piano crusher".[22] Julia Leconte of NOW stated that Legend's voice shines in the song.[23] Molloy Woodcraft of The Guardian also praised Legend's vocal talents on the song.[24] A live rendition of the song was nominated for Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards.

Live performances[edit]
On August 20, 2013, Legend performed the song live on the Late Show with David Letterman.[8] On August 27, 2013, Legend performed the song at The Box in New York City.[25] On September 2, 2013, Legend performed the song on Jimmy Kimmel Live! along with the album's second single "Made to Love".[26] On October 10, 2013, Legend performed the song during his appearance on The Wendy Williams Show.[27] The song was performed by Legend at the 56th Grammy Awards on January 26, 2014.[28] The song was also performed as a duet with Taylor Swift during her 1989 World Tour.[citation needed]

Music video[edit]
The song's music video was shot in Italy just days before Legend's wedding, featuring his fiancée, model Chrissy Teigen.[29] The video ends with footage from their actual wedding in Lake Como, Italy.[30][31] On September 12, 2013, the first image from the music video was released.[32] On October 2, 2013, the full version of the Nabil Elderkin-directed black and white music video for "All of Me" was released through Vevo on his YouTube channel.[30][33][34] The video was meant to bring the relationship full circle, as he chose the man who originally introduced them to each other, Elderkin, to direct it.[29][35]

A duet version of the song with accompanying music video was filmed with violinist Lindsey Stirling and released on YouTube on October 26, 2013.[36]

In November 2015, the YouTube video's title mysteriously changed from 'All of Me' to 'One Last Time' and then changed back.[37] The same happened on Spotify[38][39] and Google Play.[40][non-primary source needed] There has been no explanation for this incident.

As of September 2025, the music video has received over 2.5 billion views and over 13 million likes on YouTube.[41]

"All of Me" is a song by American singer John Legend from his fourth studio album Love in the Future (2013). It is dedicated to Legend's wife Chrissy Teigen.     "All of Me" first aired on American mainstream urban radio as the album's third single on August 12, 2013.

On the week ending May 17, 2014, it peaked at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming his first number-one single in the United States. It knocked off "Happy" by Pharrell Williams, which had spent 10 weeks at number one. The song peaked at number two in the United Kingdom, South Africa and New Zealand and topped the charts in Australia, Canada, Ireland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands. It became the second best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 4.67 million copies sold for the year,[1] as well as the third best-selling song in the United Kingdom.[2] "All of Me" was the third best-selling song of 2014 with 12.3 million equivalent-units worldwide (sales plus streaming), according to the IFPI.[3]

A remix of the song (Tiësto's Birthday Treatment remix), featuring EDM artist Tiësto, was released in January 2014 and won the 2015 Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical, while another remix was done in March of that year by trance artist Dash Berlin. A live version of the song was nominated for Best Pop Solo Performance, losing to Williams' "Happy".[4]

Background and composition[edit]
"All of Me" is a piano ballad, which was inspired by his then-fiancée, now wife, model Chrissy Teigen.[5] The couple met in 2007 on the set of his video for "Stereo". They were then married on September 14, 2013.[6] The song was produced by Dave Tozer and Legend himself.[7] It is a simple, modest proposal set against delicate keys.[8]

Sheet music for "All of Me" shows the key of A♭ major with a slow tempo of 63 beats per minute. Vocals span from C3 to B♭4.[9]

Release and promotion[edit]
In June 2013, Legend premiered "All of Me" during a performance on Oprah Winfrey's Oprah's Next Chapter.[10] On August 6, 2013, the full song was released to iTunes along with the pre-order for Love in the Future.[5][11] "All of Me" impacted American mainstream urban radio as the third single from Love in the Future on August 12, 2013.[12]

Dutch electronic producer Tiësto released a remix of the song in January 2014.[4] A country-influenced duet version of "All of Me" with Jennifer Nettles, featuring Hunter Hayes on guitar, was released in June 2014.[13]

Commercial performance[edit]
After being stationary at number two for six weeks, "All of Me" finally reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated May 17, 2014. This was Legend's first Hot 100 number one single, almost 10 years since his first appearance on the chart. That was the longest wait for an artist's first number-one song from their first chart appearance since Snoop Dogg waited 10 years and 10 months for his.[14][15] "All of Me" became the second best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 4.67 million copies sold for the year. The song spent three weeks at number one before being dethroned by Iggy Azalea's "Fancy" featuring Charli XCX.[1] Additionally, "All of Me" spent 23 consecutive weeks in the Billboard Hot 100's top 10 and spent an overall 59 non-consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.[16] As of April 2016, "All of Me" has sold 5,878,000 copies cumulatively in the United States.[17]

In the United Kingdom, "All of Me" peaked at number two on the UK Singles Chart,[18] and it became the third best-selling song of 2014 in the UK.[2] As of February 2016, the song has sold 1.18 million copies in the UK.[19]

Critical reception[edit]
"All of Me" was met with generally positive reviews from music critics. Ken Capobianco of The Boston Globe named the song the album's "essential track".[20] Ryan Patrick of Exclaim! said the song, shows "Legend's current commercially friendly, sentimental sound."[21] Jon Dolan of Rolling Stone called the song a "mountainous piano crusher".[22] Julia Leconte of NOW stated that Legend's voice shines in the song.[23] Molloy Woodcraft of The Guardian also praised Legend's vocal talents on the song.[24] A live rendition of the song was nominated for Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards.

Live performances[edit]
On August 20, 2013, Legend performed the song live on the Late Show with David Letterman.[8] On August 27, 2013, Legend performed the song at The Box in New York City.[25] On September 2, 2013, Legend performed the song on Jimmy Kimmel Live! along with the album's second single "Made to Love".[26] On October 10, 2013, Legend performed the song during his appearance on The Wendy Williams Show.[27] The song was performed by Legend at the 56th Grammy Awards on January 26, 2014.[28] The song was also performed as a duet with Taylor Swift during her 1989 World Tour.[citation needed]

Music video[edit]
The song's music video was shot in Italy just days before Legend's wedding, featuring his fiancée, model Chrissy Teigen.[29] The video ends with footage from their actual wedding in Lake Como, Italy.[30][31] On September 12, 2013, the first image from the music video was released.[32] On October 2, 2013, the full version of the Nabil Elderkin-directed black and white music video for "All of Me" was released through Vevo on his YouTube channel.[30][33][34] The video was meant to bring the relationship full circle, as he chose the man who originally introduced them to each other, Elderkin, to direct it.[29][35]

A duet version of the song with accompanying music video was filmed with violinist Lindsey Stirling and released on YouTube on October 26, 2013.[36]

In November 2015, the YouTube video's title mysteriously changed from 'All of Me' to 'One Last Time' and then changed back.[37] The same happened on Spotify[38][39] and Google Play.[40][non-primary source needed] There has been no explanation for this incident.

As of September 2025, the music video has received over 2.5 billion views and over 13 million likes on YouTube.[41]
